name: Gulp
summary: Streaming task runner from the era before bundlers absorbed the build.
what_it_is: A build system where tasks are written as JavaScript functions piping files through transformation streams in memory, rather than configured declaratively and written to disk between steps as Grunt did.
why_it_matters: Gulp beat Grunt because code composed better than configuration, and then bundlers made the whole category largely redundant by owning the dependency graph. It is worth knowing for a reason this project can demonstrate directly: the site you are reading about was built with Gulp 4, Bower and Foundation 6, and that build no longer installs on a current Node at all. Recognising a gulpfile tells you roughly when a codebase was last thought about.
suitable_for: Maintaining existing codebases that still build with it
Non-bundling file pipelines, such as image or asset processing chains
not_suitable_for: New frontend projects — a bundler or npm scripts cover this ground
Teams with no existing Gulp expertise to maintain the plugin chain
verifiable_facts: Official docs describe a streaming task runner configured in JavaScript.
